review.method: Explicit coding-assistant lexical/constituent review of exact N1904 Greek and displayed LSV. Inflection, syntax, repetition and witness differences checked; pending independent peer and reader review. No raw LSV Strong-tag or inferred global lexical assignments.
review.sourceTokenization: Explicit zero-based whitespace tokens including punctuation.

2:1.sourceText: Διὰ τοῦτο δεῖ περισσοτέρως προσέχειν ἡμᾶς τοῖς ἀκουσθεῖσιν, μή ποτε παραρυῶμεν.
2:1.targetText: Because of this it is more abundantly necessary to take heed to the things heard, lest we may drift away,

groups.note: The actual passive heard participle is substantival, naming the things heard; English things supports that real nominalized predicate, not an extra source things noun.
The μήποτε negative-purpose idiom is rendered lest; both actual components retain that one apprehensive connection.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual accusative us is the subject of the heed infinitive; LSV leaves that subject implicit in it is necessary to take heed. It is not reassigned to the different we subject encoded in the later drifting verb.

2:2.sourceText: εἰ γὰρ ὁ δι’ ἀγγέλων λαληθεὶς λόγος ἐγένετο βέβαιος, καὶ πᾶσα παράβασις καὶ παρακοὴ ἔλαβεν ἔνδικον μισθαποδοσίαν,
2:2.targetText: for if the word being spoken through messengers became steadfast, and every transgression and disobedience received a just repayment,

groups.note: N1904 λαληθείς is an aorist passive spoken participle; LSV being spoken preserves its speech head without establishing an ongoing speaking process.

2:3.sourceText: πῶς ἡμεῖς ἐκφευξόμεθα τηλικαύτης ἀμελήσαντες σωτηρίας; ἥτις ἀρχὴν λαβοῦσα λαλεῖσθαι διὰ τοῦ Κυρίου, ὑπὸ τῶν ἀκουσάντων εἰς ἡμᾶς ἐβεβαιώθη,
2:3.targetText: how will we escape, having neglected such great salvation? Which having received [that] spoken through the LORD [from] the beginning, was confirmed to us by those having heard,

groups.note: The actual beginning noun is the object of taking in the Greek first-proclaimed idiom; LSV keeps that same beginning head while recasting its relation as from the beginning. The added from is separately explained.

Greek ἀρχὴν λαβοῦσα λαλεῖσθαι means taking a beginning to be spoken, that is, first proclaimed. LSV literally recasts λαβοῦσα as having received and moves beginning into a temporal phrase. This exposes the actual taking/receiving head while making that altered complement construction explicit.

The actual present passive infinitive λαλεῖσθαι means to be spoken under taking a beginning; LSV prints spoken in its received-that-spoken wording. The speech head is retained with the infinitive-to-participial/complement recast explicit.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the nominal/relative support that for its received-that-spoken phrasing; Greek has a speaking infinitive, without a separate that pronoun.
English supplies from to make beginning a temporal modifier; Greek beginning is the object in taking a beginning to be spoken, without a written from preposition.

2:4.sourceText: συνεπιμαρτυροῦντος τοῦ Θεοῦ σημείοις τε καὶ τέρασιν καὶ ποικίλαις δυνάμεσιν καὶ Πνεύματος Ἁγίου μερισμοῖς κατὰ τὴν αὐτοῦ θέλησιν.
2:4.targetText: God also bearing joint-witness both with signs and wonders, and manifold powers, and distributions of the Holy Spirit, according to His will.

groups.note: The compound συνεπιμαρτυροῦντος expresses God joining in corroborating witness; English also bearing joint-witness renders that whole predicate without independent Greek also or joint tokens.

2:5.sourceText: Οὐ γὰρ ἀγγέλοις ὑπέταξεν τὴν οἰκουμένην τὴν μέλλουσαν, περὶ ἧς λαλοῦμεν.
2:5.targetText: For He did not subject the coming world to messengers, concerning which we speak,

groups.note: The actual inhabited-world designation οἰκουμένην is rendered world, retaining that head rather than a different Greek κόσμος noun.

unmappedSource.reason: The second attributive article introduces the coming modifier; LSV uses the adjective-like coming before world without an extra relative/article word.

2:6.sourceText: διεμαρτύρατο δέ πού τις λέγων Τί ἐστιν ἄνθρωπος ὅτι μιμνῄσκῃ αὐτοῦ; ἢ υἱὸς ἀνθρώπου ὅτι ἐπισκέπτῃ αὐτόν;
2:6.targetText:
and one in a certain place testified fully, saying, “What is man, that You are mindful of him,
Or a son of man, that You look after him?

groups.note: The actual indefinite locative adverb πού means somewhere; English expands it as in a certain place without independent source certain/place words.

2:7.sourceText: ἠλάττωσας αὐτὸν βραχύ τι παρ’ ἀγγέλους, δόξῃ καὶ τιμῇ ἐστεφάνωσας αὐτόν,
2:7.targetText:
You made him [a] little less than messengers,
You crowned him with glory and honor,
And set him over the works of Your hands,

groups.note: The actual lessening verb ἠλάττωσας is expanded as You made ... less around its written object/degree phrase; it is not an independently printed Greek make verb plus a separate less adjective.

The actual βραχύ τι degree/time expression means a little/somewhat or for a short while; LSV prints bracketed a with little. Both real modifiers retain this one expression without inventing a separate source time noun or resolving the duration/degree interpretation.

unmappedTarget.text: And set him over the works of Your hands
unmappedTarget.reason: Source-witness clause addition: the longer TR reading includes the setting-over-works quotation here; pinned N1904 ends the verse with crowning him and has no corresponding setting verb, works or hands phrase at this occurrence.

2:8.targetText: You put all things in subjection under his feet,” for in the subjecting to Him all things, He left nothing to Him unsubjected, but now we do not yet see all things subjected to Him,

groups.note: The actual subjecting verb ὑπέταξας is expanded as You put ... in subjection; the English verbal/nominal pieces retain one written predicate rather than invented separate put/subjection source words.

2:9.sourceText: τὸν δὲ βραχύ τι παρ’ ἀγγέλους ἠλαττωμένον βλέπομεν Ἰησοῦν διὰ τὸ πάθημα τοῦ θανάτου δόξῃ καὶ τιμῇ ἐστεφανωμένον, ὅπως χάριτι Θεοῦ ὑπὲρ παντὸς γεύσηται θανάτου.
2:9.targetText: and we see Him who was made [a] little less than messengers—Jesus—because of the suffering of death, having been crowned with glory and honor, that by the grace of God He might taste of death for everyone.

groups.note: The actual βραχύ τι expression permits degree or short-duration interpretation; LSV renders a little, retaining both actual modifiers without a fabricated separate Greek little word.
The actual perfect passive lessening participle ἠλαττωμένον is rendered was made ... less; the periphrastic English pieces belong to that one real lessening predicate.
Actual genitive article and first death noun jointly supply of ... death as the suffering qualifier. The later separate death occurrence remains distinct.

2:10.sourceText: Ἔπρεπεν γὰρ αὐτῷ, δι’ ὃν τὰ πάντα καὶ δι’ οὗ τὰ πάντα, πολλοὺς υἱοὺς εἰς δόξαν ἀγαγόντα τὸν ἀρχηγὸν τῆς σωτηρίας αὐτῶν διὰ παθημάτων τελειῶσαι.
2:10.targetText: For it was fitting to Him, because of whom [are] all things, and through whom [are] all things, bringing many sons to glory, to make the author of their salvation perfect through sufferings,

groups.note: The actual ἀρχηγός designates the originator/leader/pioneer; LSV author retains that original head, not a separate Greek writer noun.
Actual genitive article and salvation noun jointly supply of ... salvation as the author/leader qualifier. Their retains its distinct actual personal-pronoun anchor.
The actual perfecting infinitive τελειῶσαι is expanded as to make ... perfect around its object; no independent Greek make verb is invented.

saying, “I will declare Your Name to My brothers,
In the midst of an assembly I will sing praise to You”; and again, “I will be trusting on Him”;

The actual accusative You is the object of singing praise; English marks that same addressee as to You, without an independent Greek to preposition.
The actual perfect confidence/trust participle πεποιθώς at raw2:13 is paired with its real will-be auxiliary; LSV renders the state as will be trusting at2:12, not an invented present participle.

2:14.sourceText: ἐπεὶ οὖν τὰ παιδία κεκοινώνηκεν αἵματος καὶ σαρκός, καὶ αὐτὸς παραπλησίως μετέσχεν τῶν αὐτῶν, ἵνα διὰ τοῦ θανάτου καταργήσῃ τὸν τὸ κράτος ἔχοντα τοῦ θανάτου, τοῦτ’ ἔστιν τὸν διάβολον,
2:14.targetText: Seeing, then, the children have partaken of flesh and blood, He Himself also took part of the same in like manner, that through death He might destroy him having the power of death—that is, the Devil—

2:15.sourceText: καὶ ἀπαλλάξῃ τούτους, ὅσοι φόβῳ θανάτου διὰ παντὸς τοῦ ζῆν ἔνοχοι ἦσαν δουλείας.
2:15.targetText: and might deliver those, whoever, with fear of death, throughout all their life, were subjects of bondage,

groups.note: The actual article plus living infinitive nominalizes the duration of living of these same bound people; LSV renders their life, making that contextual subject/possessor explicit without inventing an independent Greek their pronoun.
The actual liable/bound adjective ἔνοχοι is rendered subjects of bondage. Subjects here names the people held liable/subject to bondage, not a different Greek citizenship or subordinate noun.

2:16.sourceText: οὐ γὰρ δήπου ἀγγέλων ἐπιλαμβάνεται, ἀλλὰ σπέρματος Ἀβραὰμ ἐπιλαμβάνεται.

2:17.sourceText: ὅθεν ὤφειλεν κατὰ πάντα τοῖς ἀδελφοῖς ὁμοιωθῆναι, ἵνα ἐλεήμων γένηται καὶ πιστὸς ἀρχιερεὺς τὰ πρὸς τὸν Θεόν, εἰς τὸ ἱλάσκεσθαι τὰς ἁμαρτίας τοῦ λαοῦ.
2:17.targetText: for this reason it seemed necessary to Him to be made like the brothers in all things, that He might become a kind and faithful Chief Priest in the things related to God, to make propitiation for the sins of the people,

groups.note: The actual obligation verb ὤφειλεν means He ought/was obliged. LSV recasts that obligation as it seemed necessary to Him; the whole modal expression retains the original owing/obligation head rather than inventing a Greek seeming verb or dative pronoun.
The actual merciful adjective ἐλεήμων is rendered kind; the actual mercy head remains distinct from a different Greek kindness adjective.

The actual nominalized τὰ πρός expression, things toward/pertaining to God, is the accusative respect/complement of the priestly office. LSV renders that whole relation in the things related to, without independent Greek in or relate words.
The εἰς plus nominalizing article introduces the purpose infinitive, rendered to make propitiation; English to retains the purpose construction without another source to word.
The actual propitiating/expiating verb ἱλάσκεσθαι is expanded as make propitiation; its English verb/noun pieces do not invent separately written Greek make and propitiation words.

The actual accusative sins noun is the object of the propitiating predicate; English recasts that same complement as for the sins under make propitiation. Its for expresses the case/governed-object relation without a separately written Greek for preposition.
